You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 05e815539f3f161585c13a9ab023341bade2c52f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wan Jiabing <wanjiabing@vivo.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Mar 2022 17:41:48 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] cxl/core/port: Fix NULL but dereferenced coccicheck error

Fix the following coccicheck warning:
./drivers/cxl/core/port.c:913:21-24: ERROR: port is NULL but dereferenced.

The put_device() is only relevent in the is_cxl_root() case.

Fixes: 2703c16c75ae ("cxl/core/port: Add switch port enumeration")
Signed-off-by: Wan Jiabing <wanjiabing@vivo.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220307094158.404882-1-wanjiabing@vivo.com
Signed-off-by: Dan Williams <dan.j.williams@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/cxl/core/port.c b/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
index c1681248f322..2ab1ba4499b3 100644
--- a/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
+++ b/drivers/cxl/core/port.c
@@ -911,7 +911,10 @@ static void cxl_detach_ep(void *data)
 			break;
 
 		port = find_cxl_port(dport_dev);
-		if (!port || is_cxl_root(port)) {
+		if (!port)
+			continue;
+
+		if (is_cxl_root(port)) {
 			put_device(&port->dev);
 			continue;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/cxl/core/port.c`**
- The code was modified to address a potential NULL dereference warning identified by coccicheck.
- The original condition `if (!port || is_cxl_root(port))` was split into two separate checks:
  - The first check now only verifies if `port` is NULL (`if (!port) continue;`), and if it is, the loop continues to the next iteration.
  - The second check (`if (is_cxl_root(port))`) now only executes if `port` is not NULL, ensuring that `put_device(&port->dev);` is only called when `port` is valid.

### Relationships
- The modification in `drivers/cxl/core/port.c` directly addresses the coccicheck warning about dereferencing a NULL pointer. By separating the checks, the code ensures that the `put_device()` function is only called when `port` is guaranteed to be a valid pointer, thus preventing potential runtime errors. This change is linked to the previous commit identified by the fix tag, which introduced the enumeration of switch ports, indicating that the issue arose from that earlier modification.

Reason: The code snippet dereferences `port` with `put_device(&port->dev);` without ensuring that `port` is not NULL. If `find_cxl_port(dport_dev)` returns NULL, the condition `!port || is_cxl_root(port)` will evaluate to true, and the code will attempt to dereference `port` in the `put_device` call, leading to a NULL pointer dereference.
